Notes

  1. 1The bath towel is linteum (Jack’s ruling, 29 October 2026), not Traupman’s gausapina, classically a frieze coat. Ruling: linteum and mantēle.
  2. 2The libellī use linteum for the tablecloth (Mart. XIV 138). Traupman (p. 125) gives mantēle, which is a tablecloth only in a post-classical sense (Lewis & Short: Isidore, Orig. 19.26.6; Trebellius Pollio). Ruling: linteum and mantēle.

Examples

  • Ē soliō ēgressum pater linteō siccāvit

    When he got out of the bath, Dad dried him with a towelLibellus VII, Diēs ūnus Osoitsae
